reasons.C: Short flat declaratives told in the first person almost throughout, no contractions and plain procedural diction; this is closest to the passage's even, unhurried rhythm, though it is a touch more fragmentary.
reasons.B: Also clipped and first person with no contractions, but small flourishes ('the dough sulks', 'It feels like help. It is not.') and a slide into general advice make it a little more performed than the passage.
reasons.D: It has the right short-sentence movement but overdoes it: lots of fragments, imperative second person and punchy aphorisms ('Hot water makes it dead', 'Longer than you want'). It reads as an imitation of the author.
reasons.A: Long compound sentences joined with semicolons, colons and subordinate clauses, in a smooth explanatory essay register. Its movement and punctuation are furthest from the passage's terse style.
